hypothesis: Edey wan pH eqqal iddikud n Hydrogen (H daɣ pH) ion tan daɣ chemical test

source: Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).
reference: Iyon tan wǝn Idrojen amosan proton tan ǝlănen elektron tan ǝd ǝzjarnen (a ǝja s atom tan wǝn Idrojen ehen proton ǝyyan d elektron ǝyyan).
hypothesis: Ions tan win Hydrogen aqqalan proton tan wi ilan electron tan nasan ijjanen fal san (daɣ as atomet tan win Hydrogen ahanen proton iyyan d electron iyyan)

source: Swirl the two dry powders together and then, with clean wet hands, squeeze them into a ball.
reference: šămaširwăy pudar tan wǝn ǝssǝn dǝhen arbiz tan akos data s tăsiɣărăd ǝfăssan ărrudnen.
hypothesis: Ijjit n issin powder tan wi eɣsan tolas s ifassaran n ifassaran, issikna s efes n tazoli

source: The moisture on your hands will react with the outer layers, which will feel funny and form a sort of shell.
reference: Tănăsmot fal ifăssan nak a tăxdam fal tăbqih tan he aqqilnen izijraz tolas eɣnin tekăkit.
hypothesis: Tazaft fal əfus iness ad təjəjəj ad təjəjəjən, ad təjəjəjən ad təjəjən sund təjəj.

source: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system.
reference: Tiɣărmăten tǝn Harappa d Mohenjo-daro ǝlănat asuj wan ăsǝrid n sălanga tan daɣ ehan fuk osăɣăn ǝd sistem ǝknan tulăɣăy.
hypothesis: Timizdaɣ tin Harappa d Mohenjo-daro ilanat toilet tan daɣ ihanan fuk, idakalan s sistem n asiflas

source: Remains of sewage systems have been found in the houses of the Minoan cities of Crete and Santorini in Greece.
reference: ǝdiršăn n sistem tan win erdan han ǝhănan win iɣirmăn win Minoan tan Crete d Santorini daɣ Greece.
hypothesis: Ijjit n sistem tan n asiwad n aman ijraw daɣ ihanan n iɣirman win Minoan n Crete d Santorini daɣ Greece

source: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
reference: Daɣ Masar tan aru Persia d addawla tan China ǝllan-t sălanga tan. Daɣ xădărat tan Roma , salanga tan amosăn ǝhănan win ăsirid n aljămăɣa daɣ artăyan meddan d deden.
hypothesis: Daɣ akal wan Roma, toilet tan alwaqqan iyyad aqqalan achrut n ihanan n asafar n addinat s id orakan addinat d tilawin daɣ taggayen n addinat

source: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
reference: Alwaq wa ǝd tăɣred awadi ehan tǝmăd n kilometir tan, satelit as tăxdămad.
hypothesis: Alwaq wa id t asawal s awadim wa izjaran i 1000 n mil, exdam s satellite

source: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
reference: Satelit daɣ ǝšinnăwan jărraw teɣare dihen ad eqqil daɣ ărmod.
hypothesis: Satellite daɣ edag ijraw alwaq wan isim tolas ikna s afalla, daɣ alwaq iyyan

source: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
reference: Satelit ikka ǝšinnăwan daɣ roket. Siantifik tan xăddamăn s teleskob tan daɣ ǝšinnăwan fal as amădal ǝsimutti annur d akăyad nanaɣ.
hypothesis: Satellit eqal atiwəjan dǎɣ edag fal raket. Əmusanan axdaman telescopetan dǎɣ edag falas atmosphère tan Akal taqal ayhan dǎɣ tabarat ən təmuqunt əd akayad.

source: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
reference: Roket măqqorat n 100 n atkul a tăddobet asuki n satelit meɣ teleskob ǝšinnăwan.
hypothesis: Awen ila asissiki ən rocket ən 100 n météritan fal adizgaran satelit meɣ télescope dǎɣ edag.

source: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
reference: Adar ămmutay daɣ alɣălim ǝmmǝkăn aqqanen eɣăf. Harat wa măqqoran hullan ǝja hannaɣ adar wen amos as ăssirɣas tolas ăssirmad asikil.
hypothesis: Taɣelit təwayad adunya dǎɣ lalan wi ogaran atiwagan. Ašanzi wa ogaran təmɣire təwayad ye nanaɣ eqal aygan ye-naɣ tamusne ogaran ogaran ogaran əd ogaran.

source: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
reference: Eway hannaɣ ǝd qităr, torfen d ǝsuj n asikil ajotnen.
hypothesis: Eqqal alwaq wa id ikfa tren, auto d isuj iyyad ajjotnen n alxidmat

source: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
reference: Emel nasan imăl-t as wǝ madroy tattan wǝ mădroynen šund a-wa ǝjan wǝ măqqornen jǝr ǝman nasan.
hypothesis: Daɣ ihandagan win, illan ti imussan n iddikud n meddan wi ittaken imudaran n meddan s tizarat har antilop tan d deer tan

source: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
reference: ǝllan-t mus tan ajotnen mădroynen (han mus tan n tammǝduwa) tattanen ǝmudăran šund xăšarat, qarid tan , ǝmăjăydaran d ǝgdad.
hypothesis: Daɣ samando, illan ti imusanan ajjotnen madroynen (har ti imusanan n aɣrim) wi ittaknen imudaran madroynen ajjotnen chund imudaran, imudaran, tiššarwen d ihanan

source: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
reference: Anăjax nasan amos tǝfert n niche ălxidmat s addobat awadim a tat ej daɣ ălɣillas n ămidiš id addinat wǝ yadnen.
hypothesis: Isid wan afanaz nasan eqqal isim wan niche, alxidmat n alxidmat n cat fuk ta taqqalat a war n ijji id wi yadnen

source: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
reference: ǝhărrăn amosan mostan w-ǝkna ǎnhirǝj ujiš hullan, ǝzzăɣnen s-tăqqimen s-ǝsmăwan nasan unhajan.
hypothesis: Lions aqqalan imusanan wi ojjaran tamazduq, izzaɣan daɣ taqqimen maqqornen s isim nasan Prides

source: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
reference: Prides ǝjan s karad meddan hak ǝd karadat tǝmirwen n ălyad d nna-ten nasan.
hypothesis: Ordinat tan tijja s iyyan har karad n imaxlaken wi ojjaran id har 30 n timaxlaken d tiw-at

source: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
reference: As tessǝd ḍeḍen ɣas anǝmmahaẓnat, daɣ-s-ǎqqal-nat ejjadaš maqqoran n-šatma d-tarǎten-s-nat.
hypothesis: Ijjit tan aqqalan a oharnen hullan s iman nasan, aqqalan ahinzazaɣ maqqoran n tiɣiswen d tilawin

source: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
reference: Prides wan ahǝr amosan šund tǝwaɣnɣwen n tǝɣis meɣ ǝdan ehare olahan ǝd ehran (war hen mus tan yădnen măqqornen) daɣ alxăl tolas aqqălnen tăwăqqas n wǝ yadnen.
hypothesis: Amaššaɣalan ən əššəɣəl aqalan sund təɣirwen ən wiššaran meɣ iməššaran, imudaran ogdahan dǎɣ təwaƭ ən əššəɣəl (mašan winan eqel iyad iməššaran maqornen) dǎɣ tamusne, əd deɣqanen eqalan ayknan ayknan ye taməte nasan.

source: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
reference: Amadaš atǝwăɣlăyan hullan, nimir addobat afton,ašăyaf, aššal n ǝddokad šajren tolas ǝkriš har sammos ǝhăndagan assăhat n ăhalis.
hypothesis: Tiger tan eqqal imusanan n tiger tan s assahat s afissar n assahat n awadim

source: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
reference: Nimir ha tăqqemt šund (Genus Panthera) tan ǝhărran,wăšil tan d jagwar tan . Mus tan wǝn akkoz ɣas addobat nen teɣărit.
hypothesis: Tiger eqqal daɣ taqqimt n tiger tan (Genus Panthera) s eqqal imudaran, leopard tan d jaguar tan.

source: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
reference: Teɣărit tan nimir war t-olah id emasli n ahar mušam šund atărmis wan Snarly.
hypothesis: Taɣawt tan tiger war t amos chund taɣawt n asisin s taɣelit net mucham t amos ach-ak n majrad n awalan s tizarat

source: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
reference: Oselot tan arhăn tetăte n ǝmudărăn wǝ mădroynen. Rămmasan kaya tan, tăššalen, nimir tan d ǝgdăd a fal addoben. Balaba ǝmudǎran fuk w-itǎhǎyut ocelot amossan at-ojjǎran tǝmmitkǎyt hullan.
hypothesis: Ocelot tan šund ad imanan imudaran madroynen. Ad ikrasan imaɣran, issiwan, imudaran d ihanan a fal addoben. Ijjit n imudaran fuk wi id izjarnen ocelot tan aqqalan madroynen hullan fal as eqqal

source: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
reference: Siantifik tan ordahan as oselot tan ǝlkăm tolas ǝjawan ehăre ikša s adu, asăraɣ n dǝha ad illan daɣ akal.
hypothesis: Imusanən ən təmusnawen aɣelan as ocelottan itajən əd ajarawnat ihishkan ye adanan (tənes) fal anəzgum, dǎɣ asikin ən edag wa dǎɣ aqalan dǎɣ akal.

source: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
reference: Addoben akyăd hullen daɣ tǝhăy s ehad tolas akir ahin ǝman net. Oselot tan rămmăsăn nimir s tulăt id ahǝnzazaɣ wa daɣ ǝzzăɣăn.
hypothesis: Ocelot tan addoben akayad hullan daɣ alwaq wan eɣaf s akayad n alwaq wan alwaq tolas imuttiyan hullan daɣ albas. Ocelot tan ikrasan imudaran nasan s anmizlay daɣ ahinzazaɣ nasan tolas izjar id imudaran nasan

source: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
reference: Alwaq wa ǝd tăqqemt andărrat n harătan ǝzzăɣnen ( ǝššăɣib ăndărran) tazun ǝd ǝššăɣib wa ǝd ǝzjăran (šund a fal ahălan s ădaɣ meɣ ejărew meɣ a fal ahonănan s edăg eynăyan ǝ- ad war răqqos ahunǝn nasan), alwaq wa hin osan ahǝn ăhinzazaɣ ǝzlăyan.wa ǝzzăyan.
hypothesis: Alwaq wa id taqqimt n haratan n tamudre (izdaɣ andarran) izlay id ichaɣib wan ezzaran s inta id izjaran (chund alwaq wa id izjar id achrut n iɣirman meɣ alwaq wa id izjar id tsila eynayan har war addobat ad izjar id) alwaq iyyan addobat nat ad aj in iman nasan daɣ ahinzazaɣ izlayan id ta s id izjaran

source: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
reference: Ahǝnzăzaɣ wen eynăyan ǝla alfăyda ten ǝzlăynen d ǝmădăšan ăjotnen ,daɣ awen ǝššăɣib wa eynayan ănhaja ǝd sămălan ǝzlăynen meɣ almud n amădaš ăssohen fal a-wa amos derhan nasan s tǝzărat.
hypothesis: Edag wen eynayan ila isuj izlaynen d imassukal izlaynen, awen ichaɣib eynayan ilzam samalan izlaynen meɣ amutti tan i ad aqqil imassukal maqqornen ohun awa ilzam nen azzaman wa id

source: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
reference: ǝššăɣib wan assuna war ămmutay , har ajudi ǝlan ălxidmat daɣ almud šund s data.
hypothesis: Tawset tan tizarat war t abeddel harkuk, ilzam nat amutti tan chund win aru

source: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
reference: Daɣ azzăman , alwaq wa ǝd isant ǝššăɣib wa eynăyan almud n ahinzăzaɣ wa eynayan, ǝssǝntan akăyad šund ǝššăɣib wa yadan.
hypothesis: Daɣ azzaman, as ichaɣib eynayan issinta ad ijjuch i ahinzazaɣ net eynayan, issinta ad iknan olah id ichaɣib iyyan

source: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
reference: Darat timad meɣ milyon tan n ǝwǝtyăn , ǝssǝn ǝššăɣiban anmăzlăyan har as war ăddoben ahhăr n ǝsǝm ǝyyan.
hypothesis: Daɣ samando, darat timad n iwityan meɣ har ajjudi milliontan n iwityan, ichaɣib tan win issin ad aqqilan anmizlay har war addoben isim nasan as eɣanni olahan

source: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
reference: Awen nijjanas tabǎḍḍawt na-iddaran daɣ ǝssin, s-almçna-ness tabǝnawt n-tǝmmaxlak aynaynen. Tabǎḍḍawt na-iddaran daɣ ǝssin ǝlzam ɣaqibat net tolas amos ašrut maqqoran n tămuttayt.
hypothesis: Tamatikwayt ten isim net speciation, s almaɣna net eqqal eɣanni n ich-ikilan eynaynen. Speciation eqqal alwazab war addobat a eɣna tolas eqqal achrut assohen n amutti

source: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
reference: Tešše tan tajǝnat adu sarrăɣan addinat tolas rămmăsnat dyoksid wan karbon zazjaran addinat (s unfas).
hypothesis: Ihishkan iknanen oxygen wa id awidan addinat tolas ijraw nen carbon-dioxide wa id awidan addinat (awen amos, affuɣ)

source: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
reference: Tešše tan tajǝnăt amans nasnat daɣ tăfukt s fotosantez.. Hak -ǝn telay.
hypothesis: Ihishkan ijraw nat ihishkan nasan daɣ tafukt s photosynthesis.

source: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
reference: Nǝja ǝhănan d ǝmălsan nanaɣ daɣ tešše. ǝjit n ǝšikša nanaɣ amos tešše. Andar s wadden tešše, ărǝzzej war has t-ǝlla tămudre.
hypothesis: Ihanan nasnat igazan daɣ ihishkan, ad təlašššən daɣ ihishkan. Əmik wa ogaran ye adal eqalan ihishkan. Awarha ihishkan, imudaran waradoben ad tamudre.

source: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
reference: Mosassaurus amos muftǎris daɣ azzǎmǎn net, dǎɣ awen war- t eha amǎttisu n hǎrat fuk, a fal wǎdden mosasur tan ǝyyǎd.
hypothesis: Mosasaurus eqal amutayan wa ogaran təmɣire ən azaman iness, izar winan ila takus, dǎɣ asikin ən iyad mosasaurus.

source: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
reference: Imusǎr net wǝ šǎjrotnen ǝjǎn amšišǎd n 70 n esen s tǝsmǎd lǎm net, id mǎjmuɣǎt t-okǎyǎt daɣ ammǎs n em net, almǎɣna n awen war t ǝlla agmod ǝ hǎrat fuk ǝtǝki fal abǎra net.
hypothesis: Tazawen net ti maqqornen ilanen 70 n iɣasan wi iknanen šikilan, id ijjit n iɣasan daɣ ehan net, awen amos as war t illa edag s addobat harat fuk ad itirf ehan net

source: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
reference: War n ǝkkes aššǎk hullan mušǎm addobǎt as ǝla elis ǝfrǎɣǎn. ǝmǎnsǝwǎn net ahǎn tan ǝgdǎd, emǎn wa mǎqqorǎn, id mǝdaydarǎn ǝyyǎd, addobǎt daɣ as eqqǎl a ǝtǎtǎn addinǎt.
hypothesis: War n ila musnat n tiditt mucham addobat ad ila awal ijjit. Ehan net eha turtle tan, issan maqqornen, mosasaur tan iyyad tolas addobat ad eqqil imudaran

source: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
reference: Tǎdlǝmt net tǝja har ajudi fal hǎrat fuk errǎsan amǎn, hak ǝd dinozor w-ǝ mǎqqornen šund T. rex war t ǝlla a dar ǝs olǎh.
hypothesis: Edag harwa haratan kul wi dazarnen aman; har dinosaur ogaran təmɣire sund T. rex war adobat ad eɣaf.

source: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
reference: Daɣ elwaq wad nezzay ăyeǧǧin daɣ ǝmekcan-nsen, Romen tan llan kaya-nsen wǝn ăzalaf war tǝwăzzayen mǝɣ war ten-nennum, hăkked ălxanzar n asuf, tăylalt, jilingid, hakked ămudar s ǝsǝm net dormus
hypothesis: Kuddeɣ as imuɣna nasan ajjotnen eqqal a ilan tanaya i addinat win Roma, imuɣna tan nasan eqqal nat haratan n imanan ajjotnen eha imudaran, tiw-at, tiw-at d ich-ikilan s isim net dormouse

source: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
reference: Hăret wa yeẓemmiẓliyen en as daɣ elwaq wa-daɣ tǝlaqqǝwǝn d tǝḍǝḍǝn tatten eqqimen ful ekursiten, midden wǝ- llănin ǝhiri ran ad eǧrawen banke tan wi fell ssansin idissan-nssen daɣ amir wan titetti.
hypothesis: Anmizlay iyyan amos as alwaq wa id addinat wi ijjanen d tamaɣluk aqqal nat alwaq wa id ehan daɣ ihanan, addinat wi ijjanen ijjan imanan daɣ edag s addoben ad izzaɣan daɣ achrut nasan alwaq wa id ehan alwaq wan imanan

source: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
reference: Ămeklu wan Romen wa yruwen wer ten-han ǝmekcan wǝ-d-ǝffalnin America mǝɣ Asia ɣur Eroba daɣ iwetyăn wǝ-d-ǝmmălnin.
hypothesis: Ifas n Roma tan aru war addobat ad eha isalan wi id izjaran i Eroba daɣ Amerik meɣ daɣ Asia daɣ iwityan win darat

source: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
reference: Cund ad ennăɣ, war kalla llan ăllun, hakked tămati tan, hakked kǝmbter tan, hakked goro, d war kalla yurem Romen wa yruwen tetate n tăylalt.
hypothesis: Almital, war ilen ahishk, war ilen tamadut, war ilen karto, war ilen cacao, war ilen Roman tan aru iknan tamăšɣult

source: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
reference: Babylonian tan eddăyen tămezgida i messawes-nsen ɣared, enta teqqal ideg wa yha măssissen wa meqquren.
hypothesis: Babyloni tan ikrasan i allaɣat nasan s aɣabad wa s itawan ehan n allaɣat

source: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
reference: Kalla hăkken eddunet tǝkutăwen ǝ massi-ssen, elfăqqitten terǝmman agaḍ n-derhan-tan n-messinsen s-ǝrit d-addǎlan.
hypothesis: Addinat ad aj infa id alxalan tolas imazaran ad akkinan i alxalan s timɣutar d timadachen

source: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
reference: Kalla tella hakk tămezgida ăfărag ămira ezzar ǝlli ǝdeg ǝhan ămmas war t-tăǧǧah ar elfăqqiten.
hypothesis: Templ tan fuk ilan aɣala n aɣabad ehan daɣ ammas tolas ehan wan ammas s imassukal ɣas ehan

source: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
reference: Amǝr ǝyen, eddăyen tower tan ulahen d Piramid, ǝtiwennăsen Ziggurats, ful ad umăsnet tămăzgidaten.
hypothesis: Alwaqqan iyyad, tiɣir tin ešwal n pyramid tan s itawan ziggurats, iday nat i ad aqqilan achrut n ihanan win alxidmat

source: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
reference: Aɣǝl wan afella wan Tower, kalla ymus ăseggăffar wan măssissen.
hypothesis: Taɣelit tan aɣalay eqal edag ən təməddurt ye alxakum.

source: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
reference: Daɣ ǝmren wǝn tukkisi daɣ Middle East, tăɣăhamt waǧir haret meqquren.
hypothesis: Daɣ azzaman wan eɣaf n Middle East, ehan war eqqel a assohen

source: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
reference: A yeǧǧin daɣ tămudri n Hebrew tukay daɣ ǝdeg amiran.
hypothesis: Tamudre tan ajjotnen n ahinzazaɣ wan ebray tan t ijja daɣ albas

source: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
reference: Kalla sănnint tǝḍiḍin daɣ ăfărag, elxăwăniten war kallad emmussen har ǝdeggăn ămiranin ful ăbăraqqa. Kala săxdămen ikkădiwen ful ădday n tiɣăhmin.
hypothesis: Tənaten aqalan ayhan dǎɣ əhu; mertay aqalan dǎɣ təmuqunen atiwajanen fal aɣalay.

source: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
reference: War kalla eǧettent tirămhitin daɣ Canaan, fulas issaɣiren eɣlănin hullan.

reference: Akǎrǎš n torfen ajotnen ewǎy id har ajudi aksǝdǎn tan ajotnen fal abǎra tan , hǎrat id ewǎyǎn s uɣna n tǎqtiya tan daɣ assexǎt ǝ amukǝn n tǝɣǝswen ǝmmǎr uɣšǎd .
hypothesis: Ajjaraw n auto tan s tiw-at eqqal id iddikud n ijji n iɣasan daɣ abara tan id eqqal id afanaz n tikarsiwen eynaynen daɣ assexat i asidu n taɣissa

source: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
reference: Omansiya tella iwetyan maqurnin, husayen daɣ agna, teffal-d daɣ idlisen cund : Goethe , fichte d Schlegel.
hypothesis: Romanticism ila harat maqqoran n cultural determinism, id izjar id imaɣran chund Goethe, Fichte d Schlegel

source: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
reference: Daɣ ǝnin n rumansiya, musnet n ikalen tekna-d miden, deffer-s yusa-d agna d idles n akal waɣ, făsus full miden war ănimenɣi, werǧi cund alqănun wi kanen ddunet, yessuheḍ, yessugda midden.
hypothesis: Daɣ almaɣna wan Romanticism, jografia t ikf-a addinat tolas daɣ azzaman ijjit alxidmaten d agna ijjan id jografia ten tolas win, s aqqalnen a ohar nen id edag wan tamazduq, aqqalan a ojjaran achareɣa tan n alxoriya

source: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
reference: Immik wa s tawassan Paris n as t amos Kapital tan azya daɣ alɣalim wan azzaman, Constantinople inta taqqal kapital ən azya tan Eroba Feodal.
hypothesis: Daɣ immik wa s Paris t amos kapital tan n alɣalim wan amarad, Constantinople t amos kapital tan n alɣalim n Eroba tan feudal

source: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
reference: Atiwazzay fal as amos edag ən taruf issintan edes ən 400 data annabi ɣisa tolas ikkimmal har awatay wan 1100 data annabi ɣisa.
hypothesis: Eqal atiwazay fal as eqal edag ən təmotayen ən tajute, eqal aywadan 400 darat J.-C. əd atiwəɣra har 1100 darat J.-C.

source: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
reference: Talɣa net tifnaz ɣur awatay wan 2000 hullan fal awa s id aqqalan assalib tan ewayan tihikkuten šund tabdoqt d darzan ilanen alqim hullan fal awa hin inachin dǎɣ hebu tan win Byzantin.
hypothesis: Edag net iddikud daɣ awatay wan 2000 fal as imuzaran win cruciade tan idlan id isuj chund silk d spices wi ijjan alqim hullan fal awa ijjan hebu tan win Byzantium

source: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
reference: Alwaq wen dǎɣ a id ifal eɣaf wan kapital tan azya Constantinople əs Paris.
hypothesis: Eqal daɣ azzaman wen as asissiki ən isim wan Kapital tan Fashion ɣur Constantinople har Paris.

source: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
reference: Tălɣa ta n lquti teqwa daɣ iwetyan n afdăn wa n 10, 11 d wa n 14.
hypothesis: Iššikil wan Gothic ijjit daɣ azzaman jir awatay wan 1000 har wan 1000 har awatay wan 1000

source: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
reference: Daɣ tizzar ăselsu ǝrtay d agna wan byzantin n asamar.
hypothesis: Daɣ santo, issədawan aqalan ayhan as tabarat tan bizantin tan egadal wan alqiblat.

source: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
reference: Full inin war llin asăɣen yeqqwan, taɣara n akal n ăfella war tuhăẓ daɣ musnet hullan sqasen-as 25 ar 30 iwetyan.
hypothesis: Hak id ijja awen, fal as illan ti tasassaɣrawt n majrad, iššikil tan win ataram addoben ad ikfan arori s 25 har 30 n awatay

source: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
reference: Ɣor tǎmmǝdawt n-wityan win jerejere, tǎssǝnta Eroba tan ǎffǎla mukina n-musner m-maness, awen iyyat daɣ tǎmmotayen timaqqornen n-alwaq wendaɣ ḍarat sǝklawan, ǝssintan addinat asaxdam n-tǝlakaten daɣ uɣan m-malsan.
hypothesis: Daɣ samando n awatay wan aru, Eroba tan ataram issintan efes n iššikil nasan

source: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
reference: Lkfaf anta taǧen ǝzăgăɣen daɣ ferǧăn full ǝni yuf daɣ titetti, illa lɣălet tăǧet terni daɣ ferǧăn n midden.
hypothesis: Aɣrim wan tamudre eqqal aɣrim s it awikkal i iji n alfayda i ad ijjuch in alfayda tan win igdiman d ihanan nasan

source: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
reference: Uzu wa lkfaf inhil hullan, anta yamus tadaɣt ta n tidet, teknent idis n idgen n ickan, imir ad gen alkfăf imir wa haḍen ad gen haret iyen daɣ tădeɣt full ad isiti ălɣellet n izăggaɣen. Anta ǝnhil,yeǧǧuḍi.
hypothesis: Aɣrim wan tamudre eqqal sistem eynaynen, alwaqqan iyyad organic, s axadam n iritan wi azunan daɣ ecoregion id amatikway n ihishkan meɣ tikarsiwen iyyad oharnen i afanaz n alfayda

source: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
reference: Daɣ tǝneqqăs, ajut n-kal šikraš n-kǎran daɣ adom n-alonan, awen daɣ ija har saden daɣ kallan ajotnen hanen tabǎrat tan tǎmotayt.
hypothesis: Daɣ attarex ijjit n imaxlaken ijja daɣ aqtisad n tamudre tolas awen har ajjudi eqqal ach-ak daɣ addawla tan ajjotnen ti ti s itaj

source: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
reference: Agna ǝyen ǧir midem wǝ llănin tikta ulănet, yuyin aɣiwăn daɣ wa llan, war ddubin ad aknen haret.
hypothesis: Subcultures tajjach nat addinat wi s afor nasan ijjan as almaɣna iyyan wi ijjan as almaɣna tan win tamazduq war n ila almaɣna tolas issiknan s afor n ta-ite

source: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
reference: W-ǝllan agna iyen, war ugdin, uẓănen full ǝwetyan a llan, iki, ideg daɣ aɣiwăn d tuzuft.
hypothesis: Subcultures addoben ad aqqilan a izlayan fal awatay, tawset, tawset, edag d/meɣ jinn wan addinat

source: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
reference: Taɣăra full ta taǧen ddunet amgired n agna anta :tawalt, tahuski, tăflest, tasertit, kaya, ideg miɣ haret wa haḍen.
hypothesis: Almaɣna tan wi ijjan as subculture t amos a izlayan addobat ad aqqil awal, aesthetic, addin, folitik, aharoj n meddan, jografia meɣ amatikway n isalan

source: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
reference: Midden wi n agna imgărăden llan ǝdrăcen-nsen miɣ imesseknen-nsen ak iyen yessan-ten cund tăwalt-nsen.
hypothesis: Addinat n subculture ajjotnen issaknen s timzal nasan s axadam n iššikil eha dumu tan, s ahanat imassukal, imuzaran d argot

source: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
reference: Abăraqa yullan full askăn n thusky n ămɣiwen daɣ ăɣrem anta asedwel n inuba, awa yeccaḍen wa kkănen miden full inuba, tiwetti n inuba wi induknin, wi waren lli daɣ aɣiwen s ɣur midden wi măqqurnin.
hypothesis: Iyyat daɣ tikarsiwen ti ojjaran s afissar n almaɣna n tamazduq eqqal as ijja fal ilyadan wi ijjanen a fal war tan-ijjil i addinat wi maqqornen alwaq wa id id id tiw-ad

source: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
reference: Niba wiɣ isem-nsen ăzuyir, haret daɣ inuba izuyiren llan qqănen-ten miden (imerrăwen-nessen), tigawt teǧrăw as imerrăwen war ddubin ad sedwellen inuba, miknasen d-essen, miɣ inuba wiɣ igraw-asen haret iyen daɣ ǝɣef miɣ tafekka-nsen.
hypothesis: "Iššikilan šund win isim nasan "awadim" meɣ eɣšad. Išikilan iyyad n awadim iknan addinat (harkuk imaɣran nasan); daɣ ihandagan iyyad, afanaz n ilyadan wen eqqal fal as imaɣran aɣbinen a fal ille awadim musnat maqqorat n ta-ite meɣ n taɣissa"

source: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
reference: Inuba ǝzuyren, wetten-ten mǝɣ găn-asen haret war ihussay s tizzar a ten-ayin imerrăwen mǝɣ ad arwălen.
hypothesis: Ilyadan wi war n ila alxoriya addoben ad ijjichan assahat meɣ assahat hullan data ad aɣan meɣ ad araman

source: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
reference: Iyyaḍ atwǎnna ǝsddǎwǎlan-tanǝd ăxuten, harat atwǎnna ǝzzǎɣan d-mannassen daɣ tǎnere.
hypothesis: Iyad aqalan aygan as aqalan aygan fal aywadan; iyad aqalan aygan dǎɣ akal fal iman nasan.

source: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
reference: As ănubi idwel ɣur ăxuten werǧi ɣur midden, inuba izuyiren mǝɣ ǝnuba iweqqăsen llan haret n idrăcen (daɣ tafekka-nsen), ǝnuba izuyiren ugdan d ăxuten cund aramaɣ miɣ war izdăy ddunet.
hypothesis: Alwaq wa id imudaran war n aqqel addinat iknan daɣ alxidmat nasan, ilyadan wi ezzaran iknan alxidmaten (daɣ alxadudan n taɣissa) oharan fuk chund win imudaran wi ijjan fal aɣil chund as eqqal a orakan meɣ a war n ila alxidmat i addinat

source: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
reference: Aselmed s allal n asenfar yuf hullan, yessinhil alamad, itag ideg ihusayen I ăselmed, scaffolding yessimɣar alamad.
hypothesis: Kuddeɣ as teɣare s ittus n project t aqqal a ti s afanaz d a ti ijjit n ta-ite, scaffolding eqqal harat har ajjudi

source: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
reference: Scaffolding warǧi haret ǝyen n ăsedwel, antan ǝtilal midden wǝ yessănen tiɣerri, wǝ d-ifalen tisdutin,wi llănin tikta ǝnayen sanen ăsexdem n ordinatur, ddubit ad knen haret yunayen.
hypothesis: Scaffolding war eqqal tikarsiwen n teɣare mucham eqqal alxidmat i addinat wi ijjan teɣare eynaynen chund axadam n program n ordinateur eynaynen meɣ asintan n tasassaɣrawt eynayat

source: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
reference: Scaffolding yeddubi ad ǝlli daɣ ǝmăn mǝɣ daɣ tidet, ămamek wa haḍen, aselmăd mǝɣ allal n ăselmed.Microsoft akked anta.
hypothesis: Iɣan adoben adiqilan ayhan əd wi dazarnen, dǎɣ salan iyad, amas ən magrad eqal əmik ən aɣan mašan eqalan amosan amosan amək ən əmik ən əmik ən magrad dǎɣ Microsoft Office.

source: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
reference: Virtual Scaffolds llan daɣ ammăs n lojisyel, knan full asesten, sigzayen-d haraten wi yessuhden hullan ad ten-iken mǝɣ a ten-yageẓ analmad.
hypothesis: Virtual Scaffolds aqalan aygan dǎɣ software əd aqalan aygan fal asistan, asisiwi əd asiwiɗ ən təmusnawen wi adobatnen adiqilan ayknan asidwal ye magrad ye adakal dǎɣ imanes.

source: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
reference: Arrăwen tǝtweggin deɣ tăɣăhămt tan tigẓa s timental ămiẓlaynin, tumasnet ǝban ăgerri d irk tigẓa miɣ amermed.
hypothesis: Ilyadan ijraw nat i aɣachod fal iddililan ajjotnen s tizarat fal as war n ila akayad, s asuj d har ajjudi as afanaz

source: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
reference: Arrăw wela ǝyyen wer yenhăgga ad yedwel deɣ ahăndeg wern ikăffeḍ, wern iteg tăɣara, wern iselmid, bucan neɣwaɣ a-wa igan.
hypothesis: War t ilzam i ilyadan ad iddikidan daɣ ahinzazaɣ war n ila afor, afor d teɣare mucham aqqalan

source: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
reference: Nakaniḍ nessan s ǝnnin ahăndeg wan tigẓa yemus ahăndeɣ n alɣfyet I windeɣ arrăwen.
hypothesis: Awen eqqal edag n aɣaf i ilyadan

source: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
reference: A-wa ităggen as inihegga ǝnnin tăzenaheṭ n tigẓa n ăseselyed ad tăwajjed ihăndeggen ulăɣnin tha ălɣafyet d imăgaẓen iwăr serhu d ăselmediknan d tigẓa tăṣuhit tădduttit.
hypothesis: Sistem wan aɣaywan n addinat eqqal a fal ikfan ihanan n eɣaf, imassukal n tayyit, teɣare n alxidmat d assexat n assexat

source: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
reference: Inihegga as tăzenahetṭn tigẓa d ăseselyeḍ ad tekf a-wa teddubet d awa yusare ehen wa deɣ t-id-newey .
hypothesis: Aɣădim n aɣălim eqqal a fal arha ad ijjich alxidmaten fuk ti ijjanen daɣ ehan wa s akăyădnen

source: The Internet combines elements of both mass and interpersonal communication.
reference: Internet asirtay haratan n-majrad ən addinat fuk d wan jir addinat.
hypothesis: Internet ehay titbaqqa n majrad n addinat d majrad n addinat

source: The distinct characteristics of the Internet lead to additional dimensions in terms of the uses and gratifications approach.
reference: Samalan wi izlaynen ən internet eway id tamɣar tan n-tisiwad dǎɣ awa id eqqalan alxidmaten d tazujišt n timzal.
hypothesis: Samalan wi ajotnen n Internet idhal nat ijjit n tiɣir n alxidmat d alfayda tan

source: For example, “learning” and “socialization” are suggested as important motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).
reference: Almital, “alamad” ad “asunin” aqqalan taxrik tan assohat nen i axadam ən Internet (James et al, 1995).
hypothesis: Almital,  teɣare  d  asidu  aqqalan isuj assohen i axadam n Internet (James d alxidmaten net, 1995).

source: “Personal involvement” and “continuing relationships” were also identified as new motivation aspects by Eighmey and McCord (1998) when they investigated audience reactions to websites.
reference: “Tajbist n awadim” d "iharojan ijlanen” intaned deɣ ejarihin Eighmey ad McCord (1998) as amosan titbaqa ikfa-neen assahat teynayat alwaq wa id ijan farak fal alwazaban n-imasajadan i Site Web tan.
hypothesis: "Tasəməwit ən adinat" ad "tənna ən tartit" aqalnat deɣ atiwasanan sund haratan aynaynen ən assəməsədu as Eighmey ad McCord (1998) ugud wa idakalan ijarawən ən iməjəjən ən intanɛt.

source: The use of video recording has led to important discoveries in the interpretation of micro-expressions, facial movements which last a few milliseconds.
reference: Asejjel n alvidyutăn ilwey-aneɣ s ideggen ămunnin n ugrih n awălan wi yeṣuhătnin d imusuten wi itag deɣtimirin mdruynin deɣ asăniya.
hypothesis: Alxidmat n akayad n video eway id afuk n afuk n micro-expressions, alxidmaten n uddim ijjan i milliseconds

source: In particular, it is claimed that one can detect whether a person is lying by interpreting micro-expressions correctly.
reference: Hllan, yeddubet awădem ad iseddettet kunta awadem isibeggut s imeskilăn win bennăn ful udem-nnit s ammek wan tidet .
hypothesis: Daɣ samalan, itkal as adobat awadim ad afissar as awadim eɣna fal afissar n micro-expressions s tiditt

source: Oliver Sacks, in his paper The President's Speech, indicated how people who are unable to understand speech because of brain damage are nevertheless able to assess sincerity accurately.
reference: Oliver Sacks, deɣ aḍris-nit The President's Speech, yesman-d ammek was addinet wi lwern gerreh awal s turna ta gen deɣ iɣet addubin ad ălmadin tidet s ămmek yeẓălen.
hypothesis: Oliver Sacks, daɣ alkittaban net The President's Speech, ikf-an immik wa s addinat wi war addoben afaham n majrad fal as ammut n ta-ite addoben ad ikf-an tiditt s tiditt

source: He even suggests that such abilities in interpreting human behavior may be shared by animals such as domestic dogs.
reference: Yeznehegga daɣ innin adabu waɣ n imuggan n addunet yeddebet ad timel akked ɣur imudaren hund iyeḍan wi nunem.
hypothesis: Ijja har ajjudi as assahat tan chund tin daɣ afissar n alxal n addinat addobat nat ad aqqilan a ilanat i arizzej chund imusanan win ehan

source: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed.
reference: Deɣ tizrăwin tǝn alqren wan 20 ăseknanet sanatet tismilin n ăniheɣ : tǝ yefarnin d ti yamunnin.
hypothesis: Umaɣ ən awatay wan 2000 isəkna as ille assin təzunawen ən təbiɗawen ən génétique: atiwaɣran əd atiwəjrawan.

source: Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation.
reference: Isata ameskel n ăniheɣ amaẓli yeynayen n ăniheɣ , d ad –tet-yekkes asekni deɣ ăggayt ta ful iga awal.
hypothesis: Amutti eɣna amutti n etari eynayan tolas nefran eɣna id amutti n etari

source: Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
reference: Azemeɣli d alas n amuken ităway-d tartit deqɣ assin iberdăn deɣ sanătet taggayin deɣ ak tăsuta.
hypothesis: Iddikud d anmizlay n amutti ijjan amutti s afalla jir issin ihanan daɣ tawset fuk

source: Out on the savanna, it is hard for a primate with a digestive system like that of humans to satisfy its amino-acid requirements from available plant resources.
reference: Deɣ ilăhin n asavana , yeṣuhet ful yaggayin tǝ ma-t-ǝn amătug wan amumezi hund awadem, ad tegrew a-wa has-yegdahen de sudar deɣ ickan.
hypothesis: Daɣ savanna, eqal ayknan ye primate dər əmik ən assəməsədu sund ən adinat ye assəməsədu ye ijitan ən amino acids ən ijitan ən ihəškan atiwəjanen.

source: Moreover, failure to do so has serious consequences: growth depression, malnutrition, and ultimately death.
reference: Sit ful awǝn wer nteg a yeclayen : tadarsi n tădawla, iban kaffuḍ d tămettant deɣ tihrăyet.
hypothesis: Daɣ asiwad, afanaz n awen ila ijji n alxidmat: tamɣare n anmizlay, tamɣare n ijjit d tamattant

source: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
reference: Isudăr n ickan wis nhil ăggaḍ-nesen han ǝfrăwen n ickan win tirewnin tiḍaɣin bucan yeṣuhet ful tăgganin hund tǝ nenɣ titaté-nesen wala asenni –nesen .
hypothesis: Isuj wi ojjaran a ti ojjaran aqqal nat protein tan wi ahanen daɣ eɣaf d legumes mucham awen ojjaran i primate tan chund net aftaɣ n afanaz fal as war n aqqel afanaz

source: In contrast, animal foods (ants, termites, eggs) not only are easily digestible, but they provide high-quantity proteins that contain all the essential amino acids.
reference: Bucan isudar n ǝmudăren (tăweṭṭuft, tamadi d tikăkitin) weggin ɣas nahil titati-nasen bucan hakken ǝsudar ulăɣnin I tafekka n awadem.
hypothesis: Daɣ anmizlay, isalan win arizzej (anɣur, termites, ifrink) war aqqel nat a ojjaran ɣas mucham iknan protein tan ajjotnen ahanen amino acids fuk wi assohat nen

source: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
reference: Haret ămdan wi ful ǝga awal, wer yemus haret maqquren innin imehwăr uren tăkărrist n isudăr hund tǝrit ta has-ǝga kaya deɣ amăgon ahel waɣ .
hypothesis: "Aɣil ən təmotayen, war eqel ayknan asəməɣrəy afal əknanen nanaɣ əntaɣəl ən "təmusne ən proteətan" dǎɣ alməɣnat iyat sund chimpinsan wi daɣ təɣrəmt ən assən.

source: Sleep interruption is the process of purposefully awakening during your normal sleep period and falling asleep a short time later (10–60 minutes).
reference: Aɣătas n ǝḍes yemus taɣara n afengumuten ǝmir wan iḍes d iḍes deɣ iḍes nḍarren (10-60 muniten).
hypothesis: Aɣil n eɣaf amos alxidmat n afanaz daɣ azzaman n eɣaf n alwaq tolas eɣes alwaq iyyan darat awa (1060 n alwaq)

source: This can be easily done by using a relatively quiet alarm clock to bring you to consciousness without fully waking you.
